mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months indicates a strengthening demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where housing starts increase consistently over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over three months signals a supply-side contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production decreases by more than 1% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% over three months signals a strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real personal consumption expenditures increase by more than 2% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure combined with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with high interest rates
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where GDP decreases by more than 1% over a quarter.
